guides.title: Record a voice note
guides.pictures: VoiceDebrief: iPhone, light, from screens.yml run 43606968488 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, v0.1.74, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: Choose who the note is for, then one button records. The recording is saved into the note while you speak, so a call or a crash cannot lose it. When you finish, the note is transcribed and debriefed on this device by Apple's models, and sent if it was for someone.

steps.caption: The Record tab, before you start.
steps.lead: This is where every note starts. First say who the note is for, because that decides what finishing does: a note for Just me stays on the device, a note for someone is sent to them, encrypted, as soon as it is written up.

callouts.text: Tap to record. It is saved as you speak.
Just me: the note stays with you.
Or choose who it is for: finishing then sends it, encrypted, when it is written up.
Or choose an audio file you already have (.m4a, .mp3 or .wav).
Your most recent notes. Tap one to open it.
The version: tap it to see what changed. Beside it, the test credit; no money is taken.

steps.caption: While recording.
steps.lead: Once you tap the button the recording is already being written into the note, so nothing is lost if a call comes in or the app is closed. You can finish with the button, with your voice, or from your headphones.

callouts.text: Tap to finish. The note is kept, then transcribed and debriefed.
Or say "send this now" or "stop recording" at the end, or press play/pause on headphones.
Finish and send in one press, to the person chosen before you started.
How long you have been recording. Everything so far is already kept on the device.
The words as you say them: a preview. The transcript that is kept is made from the recording.
Discard, if you do not want this recording. It asks first.

guides.title: Open a note: listen, send, save
guides.pictures: VoiceDebrief: iPhone, light, from screens.yml run 43606968488 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, v0.1.74, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: A note opens with its one sentence as the heading, then what has happened to it, the recording, the transcript and the debrief. Everything you can do with it is on this screen.

steps.caption: The top of a finished note.
steps.lead: A note opens on its one-sentence summary, then what has happened to it. This is the screen to check that a note was kept, sent or saved, and to listen to it again.

callouts.text: The note in one sentence, written by Apple's model on this device.
What happened to it: kept on this device, sent to whom and when, saved to which vault.
Play the recording. Tapping a line of the transcript plays from that moment.
Share or save the recording, for example to Files. It leaves the device unencrypted.
Send it: one button per recipient, encrypted to their key on this device.

steps.caption: The end of the same note.
steps.lead: Further down are the things you do less often: the clean-text experiment, saving to a particular vault, running the note again in another language, and deleting it.

callouts.text: Write a clean text: an experiment that rewrites the note as full sentences, using your own words from Settings.
Which vault to save into.
Save this note to the vault, encrypted, as one signed commit. Finished notes are saved on their own unless that is switched off in Settings.
Transcribe and debrief again, in the language chosen now.
Delete the note from this device. It asks first.

steps.caption: The Library tab.
steps.lead: Every note on this device, newest first, by day. Each row says what the note is doing right now or what you can do with it, so you can see at a glance whether anything needs you.

callouts.text: Waiting its turn: notes are written up one at a time, and you can keep recording meanwhile.
Being written up now.
Finished, and sent to somebody.
Interrupted: the recording is kept. Open it and run it again.
The Library tab, from anywhere.
The talk button, on every screen: speak to the app instead of tapping.

guides.title: Vaults: your notes, encrypted, on the device first
guides.pictures: VoiceDebrief: iPhone, light, from screens.yml run 43606968488 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, v0.1.74, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: A vault is an encrypted, version-controlled folder you own. It is made on this device and needs no server and no network. A server is a remote you can push it to, so that it is kept elsewhere as well.

steps.caption: The Vaults tab.
steps.lead: A vault is an encrypted, version-controlled folder you own. It is made on this device and needs no server; adding a server later keeps a copy elsewhere.

callouts.text: Your vaults, and where each one is: on this device only, or on a server too.
A name for a new vault.
Create a vault: a random key, made and kept on this device.
Servers you can push a vault to. The access token is kept in the Keychain.

steps.caption: Inside a vault.
steps.lead: Inside a vault you can see where it lives, push it to a server or pull from one, and check its latest commit and signature. Each saved note is a folder in it.

callouts.text: Where it lives: on this device only, or also on a server.
Choose a server to push to and pull from. Neither ever overwrites: if both sides changed, it says so and stops.
The latest commit, and its signature checked.
The files in the vault: each saved note is a folder of debrief, transcript, run and audio.

guides.title: Contacts: send a note to somebody
guides.pictures: VoiceDebrief: iPhone, light, from screens.yml run 43606968488 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, v0.1.74, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: A contact is a person, another device or an agent session that has given you their link. A note sent to them is encrypted on this device to their key: nobody else can read it, including the server that carries it.

steps.caption: Contacts, Recipients.
steps.lead: A contact is anyone who can receive a note: a person, another device or an agent session. You add one by their QR code or link; what you send is sealed to their key before it leaves.

callouts.text: Built into this test build: Claude (developer), who can read what you send. It asks before sending.
Somebody you have added.
Add somebody from a picture of their QR code, or scan it with the camera.
Or paste their link. It can only write to their inbox: it cannot read anything.

guides.title: What happened since you last looked
guides.pictures: VoiceDebrief: iPhone, light, from screens.yml run 43606968488 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, v0.1.74, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: When you open the app, a card on the Record tab says what is new: an update, with a link to what changed, and what happened to your notes since you last opened it. The app works it out from the library; it is not written by a model. The Guide's What is new lists every version, with those you skipped marked.

steps.caption: The briefing card on the Record tab.
steps.lead: When you open the app after an update, or after time away, this card says what changed and what happened to your notes. It is worked out by the app from the library, not written by a model.

callouts.text: The app was updated: tap to see what is new in this version, in the Guide.
What happened since you last looked: new notes, interrupted ones, sends and saves.
Dismiss it. The card is worked out again each time the app opens.

Save each finished note to a vault, on by default.
Which vault: the first one, or one you choose.
More holds Settings, Identity, Credit and the other sections.

guides.title: SGit Vaults: open a vault you were sent, or make one
guides.pictures: SGit Vaults: iPhone, light, from sgit-app-screens.yml run 43606971217 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: SGit Vaults keeps photos, videos, large files and secrets in encrypted vaults that a teammate can open. A vault you create is kept on this device and needs no account, no access key and no network until you share it.

steps.caption: The first screen.
steps.lead: The first screen of SGit Vaults lists your vaults and everything else the app holds: secrets, questions from the people building it, the Guide and the gallery.

callouts.text: A shared vault: on the server, and you can add and change.
A vault only on this device, not shared with anybody.
Secrets: passwords, passcodes, Wi-Fi and keys, kept encrypted in vaults.
Questions for you, from the people building the app: answer by typing or speaking.
Guide and what is new: what changed in each version and how each part works.
Gallery: vaults to show somebody, opened inside the app. Adding a vault you were sent and creating one are further down.

steps.caption: Add a vault you were sent.
steps.lead: If someone sent you a vault, this is where it goes in. What you paste decides what you can do: a vault key can add and change, a read key can only look.

callouts.text: Paste the vault key, read key or link you were sent.
A read key can only look. To add files to a shared vault you also need an access key for the server, which is not part of the vault key: ask whoever sent it.
Your own name for the vault, on this device.

guides.title: SGit Vaults: inside a vault, and its history
guides.pictures: SGit Vaults: iPhone, light, from sgit-app-screens.yml run 43606971217 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: A vault holds folders and files, like a folder on a computer, with every change kept as a signed commit.

steps.caption: A vault.
steps.lead: A vault looks like a folder on a computer. The line at the top tells you whether everything in it has reached the server, which matters before you tell a teammate it is there.

callouts.text: Whether everything is on the server, on this device only, or on its way in.
Folders, with how many files and how large.
Files: a picture shows a thumbnail. Tap one to open it, save it or share it.
Add photos, videos or files.
Share the vault with somebody.
More: history, saving a folder out, and the rest.

steps.caption: History.
steps.lead: Every change to a vault is kept as a signed commit, so you can see who added what and when, and that nobody has altered it since.

callouts.text: Each change, newest first, grouped by day.
Who made it: this device, or another.
Each change is signed, and the signature is checked.

guides.title: SGit Vaults: share a vault, and create one on the server
guides.pictures: SGit Vaults: iPhone, light, from sgit-app-screens.yml run 43606971217 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: Sharing gives somebody the vault's key. Whoever holds it can read everything in the vault, including its history, and it cannot be taken back: give it to people, not to places.

steps.caption: Share.
steps.lead: Sharing gives someone the vault's key. Read the warning first: whoever holds the key can read everything in the vault, and it cannot be taken back.

callouts.text: Send the way in: a message with the key, a link for a browser and the steps for the person receiving it. Send it only by a channel you trust.
What a key can do, said before you see it.
The vault key: read and write.
The read key: read only.

steps.caption: Create a vault.
steps.lead: A new vault is made on this device. Turn on Share it to put it on the server straight away; leave it off to keep it here until you choose to share.

callouts.text: A name, for you. The key is made here and kept on this device only.
Share it: put it on the server at once. Off, it stays on this device until you share it.
The access key the server needs to take a new vault, kept in the Keychain.

guides.title: SGit Vaults: secrets, kept in a vault
guides.pictures: SGit Vaults: iPhone, light, from sgit-app-screens.yml run 43606971217 on work/sherpa at 0f2e6f8 (the same tree as dev, 14 November 2026), after the design session's restyle.
guides.intro: A secret is a password, a Wi-Fi network, a server or a card, kept as one encrypted file in a vault, behind Face ID. A secret in a shared vault is seen by everyone who holds that vault's key, and each change is a signed commit.

steps.caption: The Secrets list.
steps.lead: Secrets are passwords, Wi-Fi networks, servers and the like, each kept as an encrypted file in a vault. Those in a shared vault are seen by everyone who holds its key.

callouts.text: Your own secrets, in a vault of your own.
Each kind has its own fields: a device, a website login, a Wi-Fi network, a server.
Who can see them: every device and person with this vault's key.
A team vault's secrets, listed under its name.
Search by name, website or user.
Add a secret.

steps.caption: One secret.
steps.lead: One secret, with its fields. Hidden values stay masked until Face ID; every change is a commit, so an earlier version is never lost.

callouts.text: Each field, with a button to copy it.
Hidden values stay masked.
Show hidden values, after Face ID.
Which vault it is kept in, when it changed and by which device.
Delete it: a commit like any other, so the vault's history keeps the earlier versions.

steps.caption: Questions for you.
steps.lead: The people building the app ask the owner questions here, and the answers go back to them encrypted. It is how decisions reach the code without a meeting.

callouts.text: Questions from the people building the app. Answer by choosing, typing or speaking; answers are encrypted to the developers' key.
How many are waiting.
Tap one to answer it.
